answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when each agent must continuously generate a unique cryptographic plume of verifiable hashes, which peers check against a shared glacier of immutable checkpoints held in a decentralized lagoon of validating nodes. An attacker creating multiple fake identities must expend genuine computational resources for every additional plume, as reuse or simulation is detectable and leads to rejection, making large-scale Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive in energy and time.
